costNote: Making the chips — wafers, packaging, testing. Revenue grew so much faster (+40%) that gross margin widened 520bp to 67.3%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next analog, mixed-signal and power chips — ADI's core long-term bet.

opex.name: Selling, marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales engineers, distribution and head-office costs.

opex.name: Amortization & special items, net
opex.note: $188M of amortization on past acquisitions (mainly Maxim), partly offset by a $24M net special-charges credit this quarter.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.note: Factory automation, aerospace, energy and test gear — about half of revenue and up 53% as the industrial recovery met AI infrastructure demand.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Chips for EVs and in-car electronics. Up 16% — the slowest of the big three this quarter.

segments.name: Communications
segments.note: Nearly doubled (+84%) on data-center demand — the AI build-out pulling ADI's power and connectivity chips into servers.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Chips for phones, wearables and gadgets. Up 6%.

takeaways.text: A record quarter: revenue up 40% to $4.02B, operating income nearly doubled to $1.61B (40.1% margin), and management guided to a record Q4.
takeaways.title: AI demand lit the fuse

takeaways.text: Communications revenue — the bucket that holds data-center sales — grew 84%. Industrial, still the biggest bucket, grew 53%.
takeaways.title: Data centers are the growth story

takeaways.text: Shareholders got $1.7B back in the quarter via dividends and buybacks; trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was $4.9B, 36% of revenue.
takeaways.title: Cash machine running

verdict: A record quarter: the AI data-center build-out plus an industrial recovery pushed revenue up 40% and nearly doubled operating profit.
